13033.details:
For Time
10,000m Bike
AND
10 Rounds (5ea)
15 Wall Ball Shots
200′ Dual KB Farmer Carry
13033.notes:
In this workout, BOTH partners are working at the same time.
Partner A will complete 1 round of 15 Wall Balls and a 200 foot carry, while Partner B is accumulating distance on the bike. Then switch places: Partner B does 1 round while Parnter A bikes. Continue in this fashion until both tasks are complete.
If you finish one element before the other, simply continue trading off with what you have left until it’s done!
Challenge yourself on the wall ball weight/height and the carry weight.
Grit it out on the bike and share the work.
Ride into your bright 2026 future with your CFSBK community!

13035.details:
For Time:
500m Row
40 Air Squats
30 Sit Ups
20 Push Ups
10 Pull Ups or Bar Muscle-Ups
13035.notes:
We did this workout on 4/30/25 and 12/16/2024!
Improvements in our fitness (work capacity across broad time and modal domains) should not be based on opinion. Retesting workouts is one way we measurably evaluate if our training inside the gym and recovery and lifestyle habits outside of it are delivering the results we’re aiming for.
If you’ve done this before, look over your training notes. Can you hold the movement standards and beat your previous time? Or, if you were scaling, possibly perform the workout as prescribed today?
This is one workout of many you’ll do this year, and as such, it’s just one data point. Give it your best, reflect, and then move forward!
Intent: < 7 min. Start at the top and work your way down. Pull ups can be strict or kipping, athlete’s choice.
Find the fastest pace you can move at today on your gymnastics without shorting your ranges of motion.

13035.details:
3-5 Rounds for Load and Quality
4 Weighted Strict Chin Ups OR 8 ea Three Point DB Row
6-8 ea Single Arm DB Bench Press @ 30×1
6-8 ea Single Leg DB RDL
16 Alternating Seated Pike Overs, 8 ea
13035.notes:
Start with moderate loads in round 1. Then make sure at least 2 of your sets today are RPE 8.5+
Athlete’s choice on the upper body pulling movement.
If balance is prohibitive on the RDLs, use a rig for light support. You can use one DB/KB in the contralateral hand, or use one weight in each. If you’ve never tried this with the top knee bent, give it a go today!
The pike overs are all about hip flexor strength, “compression” of torso to legs, and body control.

13040.details:
For Time
100 “Curtis P’s” (115/75lb)
*Starting at 0:00 and every minute on the minute, perform 4 Burpees
13040.notes:
1 “Curtis P” =
1 Power Clean +
1 Front Rack Reverse Lunge, each side +
1 Push Press
Athletes alternate who is working on each minute.
At 0:00: Partner A performs 4 Burpees + as many Curtis P’s as possible in the remainder of the minute.
At 1:00: Partner B performs 4 Burpees + as many Curti’s P’s as possible in the remainder of the minute.
Continue in this fashion until 100 total reps are completed as a team.
Scale volume and/or load so you can complete at least 3 reps of the complex per minute when it’s your turn.
Have a game plan—don’t wing it. Mindless transitions will steal your time to work. Put hands on the bar immediately after the burpees.
Barbell should be relatively light load that you can move without struggle through the whole complex.

Tomorrow we have running, strict chin-ups, rowing, and carries.
Athletes can superset their main lift with a non-interfering movement as desired.

Gorilla Rows: No prescribed load. Choose something challenging that you can move through consistent, full range of motion for 45 seconds straight. Maintain a strong hinge and stable core while keeping the movement strict and controlled.

Run < 2 min. Scale to 130m.

Row < 2 min
Dips: 1-2 sets. Do not sacrifice range of motion as you fatigue.
A. Ring
B. Matador
C. Box (foot assist)

13046.details:
Power Clean and Jerk
A. 5 sets x 2 Reps, building
B. 1 min AMRAP @ 80-85%
13046.notes:
After 2-3 lighter warm-up sets, take 5 working sets to build on a double power clean and jerk. Work to a moderately heavy, technically sound top set.
These reps are not intended to be cycled; reset the bar to the floor after the first jerk, take 5-10 seconds, and then start your second rep.
Push jerk is suggested, but athletes confident with the split jerk can feel free to employ that variation as well.
After your 5 working sets, rest a few minutes. Then complete as many reps as possible in 1 minute at 80-85% of your top weight for the day. We recommend quick singles here, but you could also practice your barbell cycling technique.

Perform 3-4 warm-up sets, then work up through three progressive sets working towards a heavy triple. Leave 1 rep in reserve. Afterwards, take 75-80% of your best lift and do a max effort set, keeping 0-1 reps in reserve.

13048.details:
Every 2:30 x 6 sets
5-15 Toes to Bar
10/8 Cal Bike
13048.notes:
Intent is to work our strength and skill under controlled fatigue!
Advanced athletes (already doing 10+ TTB unbroken consistently in metcons) should aim for the RX calorie target and on the high end of the TTB range.
Those building endurance with the skill or consistent mechanics should plan to scale back the bike in order to finish each round in under 1:15 each time in order to get ample rest before performing the skill again.
Use this progression to scale:
Intensity: Aim for big unbroken sets, staying shy of failure
Consistency: 1-2 submaximal sets of linked kipping TTB (ex: 2×3 or 1×7) or partial ROM reps
Mechanics: 5 Strict Toes to Bar or Hanging Leg Raises + 5 Kip Swings

13048.details:

A2. Pike Ups, 3-4 x 12-15
13048.notes:
Rollouts: Use a slow, controlled tempo. Maintain a hollow body position throughout the set. Only go as far as you can maintain tension.
Pike Ups: This is all about compression (torso to legs) and hip flexor/quad strength. Can be done feet together, straddle, or one leg at a time! Mix and match as desired, as long as you work with control, not momentum.

The percentage recommendations are based off of a 1 rep max for experienced lifters. If you don’t know your 1RM, simply start at light weights and go by feel through the 8 total sets of work.

Perform 3-4 warm-up sets, then work up through three progressive sets working towards a heavy triple, though not a max. Leave 1 rep in reserve. Afterwards, take 75-80% of your best set from today and do a max effort set, keeping 0-1 reps in reserve.

Intensity: Perform the workout as prescribed. You can complete a mix of strict and kipping* HSPU reps, as desired.
Consistency: Use RPE 7-8 for your rows. Perform 1-2 sub-maximal sets of HSPU per minute to accumulate volume through the workout.
Mechanics: Use RPE 6-7 for your rows . Perform 1-2 sets of Box Piked HSPU or Heavy DB Push Presses.
*Pre-requisite to kip in the workout is at least 1 strict full range of motion rep.

12+ unbroken reps: perform as RX’d
5-10 unbroken reps: accumulate 10-15 reps per round, in as few sets as possible (ex: 9/6)
3-5 unbroken reps: accumulate up to 10 reps per round, breaking as needed (ex: 3/3/3)

If you are not yet doing bodyweight strict pull-ups, perform 5-10 foot assisted reps + 5-10 (optional) kip swings per round.

Work in teams of four athletes. Three athletes will work at the same time, while one is resting.

The athlete performing the couplet can only begin their work when the next two athletes have picked up their implements!
Continue in this fashion for 5 rounds each athlete, 20 rounds total.

13793.notes:
Helen is considered to be one of the original staple CrossFit benchmark workouts. It was first programmed on CrossFit.com in August 2003. Helen was the first classic benchmark workout that included running. It was the first benchmark workout that had all three major movement modalities of monostructural, weightlifting, and gymnastics , and it was the first benchmark that is a task-priority triplet.
When this workout was first published, the fastest posted time was 8:25 by Greg Amundson. Currently, the fastest times for this workout are under 7 minutes, and high-level athletes will pace it similarly to running a mile as fast as possible. Striving for successful completion in under 15 minutes is typically a great goal to achieve, regardless of performing the workout as prescribed or scaling it. This workout challenges cardio-respiratory endurance, stamina, pull-up capacity, and grip strength.
“Helena” was introduced as a beefed up version of “Helen” for the 2023 CrossFit Games. Switching the Kettlebell Swing for a snatch (easier to judge) and increasing the gymnastic skill from pull-ups to bar muscle-ups. Jeff Adler finished in 7:56, can you beat him?

13988.notes:
Today’s workout allows us to accumulate a high volume of work via small sets and manageable intervals. The intent is that you can complete at least 3 rounds per interval.
TTB: If you can do…
5+ unbroken, perform RX
1-4 unbroken, do 3 per round (practice cycling reps as much as possible)
0 reps, do 3 strict hanging knee to chest + 5 kip swings
*If you prefer not to kip, perform 3 strict TTB OR 3 Incline TTB
DU: If you can do…
30+ reps unbroken, perform RX
10-20 unbroken, do 10 per round
1-10 unbroken, do 10 per round, counting any misses as makes
0 reps practice for 20-30 seconds each time you get to the rope

13994.details:
Every 2 Min x 5 Sets
1 Snatch Balance + 1 Overhead Squat
13994.notes:
Use these 5 sets as a technique primer for your snatches today.
Suggested RPE 5-7/10. Use loads that allow you to train aggression, balance, timing and confidence for receiving the snatch.

Suggested RPE 7-8+
After the first rep, reset the bar to the floor. Take 5-10 seconds between the two lifts, aiming to reinforce what went will in your first rep or shore up a technique error that may have occurred.

40 sec each side Contralateral Carry
10-15 each side Copenhagen Raises
13994.notes:
Carry: choose loads that allow you to stabilize your best possible overhead position for the duration of carry. Start with your more difficult side overhead.
Rest as needed between sides and exercises; each set should be completed under 5 minutes.

13996.notes:
Track back in your training notes to Week 1; this is the same protocol.
Perform 3-4 warm ups followed by 2 work sets of 5 reps at RPE 7-8. This means you have ~2-3 reps in the tank, not much more.
For the final set, go for as many reps as possible. Leave 0-1 in the tank.
The sets can be building or across. Focus on the effort involved, and make adjustments up or down in loading as needed.

13996.details:
2 Rounds for Time
500m Row
400m Run
80ft DB Suitcase Walking Lunge (50/35lb)
13996.notes:
Find a sustainable pace for your row and run, and then explore your mental toughness and grip endurance on the lunges.
Row < 2:30, scale to 400m
Run < 2:30, scale to 270m
The lunge weight needs to be heavy enough that you likely need to break it up at least once during the 80ft segment.

14008.details:

A. Strict Press

14008.notes:

14008.details:
For Time:
30 American KB swings (24/16kg)

30 American KB swings
14008.notes:
Where do you go when the going gets tough? Have a plan for what you’ll do with the feeling that inevitably pops up when you’ve done 10 burpee box jumps and have ::checks notes:: 30 reps left.
Your mind and body are both a part of training. Acknowledge it, work with it, and see what’s possible.
KB: Scale to a load you can do at least 15 reps unbroken.
BBJ: Scale to a height you can complete at least 8 reps per minute at a sustainable, not threshold, pace. Make sure to hit full hip and knee extension at the top of every rep today.

14010.details:

100 Push-ups
100 Sit-ups
100 Air Squats
14010.notes:
This classic CrossFit Benchmark chipper will push your muscular stamina while being metabolically taxing. Complete all of the pull-ups before moving to the push-ups, and so on.
There are over 85,000 logged results for this workout on Beyond the Whiteboard! See what the community is capable of here.
Try to avoid any one exercise taking more than 8 minutes.
Pull-Ups: If you can do an unbroken set of…
10+ kipping, do RX
6-8 kipping, do 75 reps
2-5 pull-ups (any), do 50 reps
If you cannot yet perform strict pull-ups, do 50 Ring Rows (tough angle)

10+, do RX.
6-8, do 75 reps
3-5, do 50 reps. Mix floor/elevated if needed.
If you cannot yet do a push-up from your feet, do 50 Elevated.

1 Segmented Snatch Pull

14018.notes:
Segmented Snatch Pull: Pause for one full second at three positions: 1″ off the floor, at the knee knee, and mid-thigh. Then complete the snatch pull, driving vertically and finishing tall.
Use moderate loads that provide feedback while allowing for proper position and balance throughout the whole lift. Consider this a “primer” before the full lift.
Snatch: Build across the 6-8 sets, using moderate to heavier loads, as technique allows. These are full/squat snatches.

5-7 ea Back Rack Reverse Lunges
14018.notes:
Track back to Week 4 and aim to go a bit heavier. After 1-2 warm-up sets, perform 4 work sets.
Perform all 5-7 reps of the lunge on one side before moving to the other. Rest as needed between sides.
The lunge loading can be progressive or sets across. Either way, aim for at least 2 sets at RPE 8+.
If you’d like to superset with a simple bodyweight movement, feel free!

14020.details:
2 Sets:
4:00 Row or Ski
3:00 Recovery
4:00 Bike
3:00 Recovery
14020.notes:
Today’s workout is about sustained effort and endurance, rather than a score for max reps. Find a pace you can hold steadily across the interval instead of sprinting the first minute. If you wear a heart rate monitor, aim to spend most of your work periods at 85-90% of your HR Max. In the recovery, try to come down to ~60-70%.
Row Pacing:
Use a split that is ~3–8 seconds slower than your 2,000m average.
We last tested our 2K Row on 6/25/26.
Example A:
2K time is 7:56
Average split = 1:59/500m.
Row at 2:02-2:07 for these intervals.
Example B:
2K time is 8:45
Average split = 2:11/500m.
Row at 2:14-2:19 for these intervals.
If you don’t know your 2K time, start by rowing at a pace you could sustain for 10+ minutes. If you get through the first interval without deviating, increase pace slightly for second set.
Bike:
Start at a pace you could sustain for 10+ minutes. Watch RPMs or Watts. Aim to hold a consistent number for the entire interval. Make adjustments as needed. Repeat for second set.
Recovery Period: Continue moving on the machine for 2 minutes at a lighter effort. In final minute, get up, shake it out, and transition to the next machine.

14020.details:
3 Progressive Sets
8-10 ea Three Point DB Rows OR Strict Chin-Ups
12-15 ea Single Leg Calf Raise*
14020.notes: We have C&J and Toes to Bar tomorrow. If you were here Sat/Mon, do DB rows today.

14022.details:
2 sets x 3 Power Clean and Jerks
2 sets x 2 Power Clean and Jerks
3 sets x 1 Power Clean and Jerk
14022.notes:
Use today’s work to set yourself up for success on the Metcon. In the first 2-4 sets, practice cycling the barbell from overhead, maintaining mid-foot balance and regaining your hook grip. On the singles, build to a weight heavier than what you’ll use in the metcon to dial in your aggression, timing, and confidence.
Plan to complete one set about every 2 min.

Barbell: light-moderate load you could cycle a few reps with, but might choose singles in the workout to stay consistent. Using ~60-70% of a 1RM is a decent guideline.
Masters 55+ = 115/65lb

3-5 unbroken: consider scaling 2-4-6-8-10-etc.
Strict: do 1-3-5-7-etc.

Ring Dips

This potent couplet pairs a challenging weightlifting movement with a high skill gymnastics movement. Elite times in this workout can be sub 4:00, however most folks will be around 6-10 minutes and can scale for that timeframe goal.
Cleans

Steady singles are fine, as well as touch and go sets.
135/115/95/75/55/-

14041.notes:

Push the pace on your runs today and keep your work inside the gym deliberate.

14043.notes:

225/180/145/130m
